verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Schedule Artemis III When 2027'; R3: 'launched by mid-2027'; R5: Artemis III mission described with 2027 context from NASA.
verifications.reasoning: Direct support from NASA sources (R1, R5) and Guardian reporting NASA (R3) for mid-2027 target.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... commercial landers... launch crew in the Orion... test rendezvous and docking capabilities'; R5: identical description.
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in NASA sources for crewed LEO rendezvous/docking test with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference ties Artemis III schedule specifically to April 2026; R2 dated April 2026 discusses only Artemis II.

verifications.claim: As reported by Space.com, the Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'The Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS rocket'; no Space.com source present.
verifications.reasoning: Fact supported by NASA sources, but attribution to Space.com unsupported as no such cited reference exists (SpaceNews R4 is different).

verifications.claim: As reported by Space.com, the Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'test rendezvous and docking... with one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R4: 'SpaceX Starship... lunar lander'; no Space.com.
verifications.reasoning: Docking with SpaceX lander (Starship in R4) supported vaguely, but specific attribution to Space.com unsupported.

verifications.claim: As reported by Space.com, Artemis III does not immediately land on the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'demonstration mission in low Earth orbit'; R3: 'no longer aim to land on the moon... low-Earth orbit'; no Space.com.
verifications.reasoning: No lunar landing (LEO test) clearly supported, but attribution to Space.com unsupported.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the Artemis III mission revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'radical changes... technical glitches and criticism... too risky'; R4: 'changing the scope... if key elements suffer major delays... Starship progress'.
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly link revisions to tech delays and risks.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'delays in hardware... SpaceX... Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander'; R3: general 'technical glitches... too risky' without HLS specificity.
verifications.reasoning: R4 supports HLS (Starship) delays; R3 supports revisions broadly but not HLS explicitly.

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... Artemis IV mission would set out... to land on the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement shifting landing to Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'.
